topics.title: How do you optimize large lists?
topics.html:
• Virtualization: react-window or @tanstack/react-virtual. Only render visible rows.
  • React.memo on list items with expensive render.
  • useDeferredValue for filter input — typing stays smooth.
  • Stable keys — DB id, not array index.
  • Infinite scroll via React Query's useInfiniteQuery.
Core Web Vitals — LCP, INP, CLS?
LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): main content load speed. INP (Interaction to Next Paint): responsiveness — avoid blocking main thread. CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): visual stability — set width/height on images.
When does React.memo NOT help?
Props include objects/functions not stabilized with useMemo/useCallback. Component uses useContext — memo doesn't stop context-driven re-renders. Render is already cheap.
What is hydration mismatch?
Hydration: React attaches event handlers to server-rendered HTML. Mismatch: server/client rendered different output. Causes: Date.now(), Math.random(), browser-only APIs without checks, locale formatting.
💬 Say it like this

The first thing is virtualization: render only the rows that are visible. That is the change that actually matters — memoizing rows in a list of ten thousand items does not help if you still create ten thousand DOM nodes.

After that I memoize the row component, use stable keys from the database id, and keep the filter input smooth with useDeferredValue. And I profile before and after, so I can say what the improvement was.

topics.title: LCP, INP, and CLS — how do you measure performance real users feel?
topics.html:
Core Web Vitals describe different parts of the experience. A fast server response alone does not establish that a page is fast or stable.

  • LCP measures when the largest eligible content is rendered. The good threshold is at most 2.5 seconds.
  • INP measures responsiveness across qualifying interactions. The good threshold is at most 200 milliseconds.
  • CLS measures unexpected visual movement. The good threshold is at most 0.1; it is a score, not a duration.
  • Assess the 75th percentile of real visits, considering mobile and desktop separately. A single Lighthouse run is a useful laboratory diagnostic, not the complete field result.

Investigate the metric that actually regressed: request discovery and render delay for LCP, long main-thread work for INP, and missing space reservations or late content insertion for CLS. Use the same route and release breakdown when comparing changes.

import { onCLS, onINP, onLCP } from 'web-vitals';

function recordMetric(metric) {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({
    name: metric.name,
    value: metric.value,
    rating: metric.rating,
    id: metric.id,
  });
  navigator.sendBeacon('/analytics/web-vitals', payload);
}

onCLS(recordMetric);
onINP(recordMetric);
onLCP(recordMetric);
In plain words

I separate loading, responsiveness, and visual stability, then measure the slow end of actual user visits. Lab tools help explain a regression; field data tells me who experiences it and whether the fix helped.

Can a page have good LCP but poor INP?
Yes. The main content may appear quickly while expensive filtering, hydration, or other main-thread work delays later interactions. Improving one metric does not automatically improve the others.
Why might a visit have no INP result?
A visit needs a qualifying interaction to produce INP. Missing interaction data is not equivalent to a measured zero; the aggregation needs to handle that distinction.
